section_summary: This section largely records Japanese notifications of warship construction and completion under the London and Washington naval treaties, followed by State Department acknowledgments and notices to the Navy Department. It also contains consular reports on Japanese naval policy and possible iron ore purchases, plus correspondence over proposed Westinghouse propulsion equipment for a Japanese cruiser.

subfiles.title: File note on Tokugawa’s Quebec speech
subfiles.about: Points to a report on the Japanese Minister’s argument for a stronger defensive navy.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references despatch 339 in file 701.9448/85.

subfiles.title: Japan entitled to build up stronger defensive fleet
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese Minister Tokugawa’s address to the Quebec Military Institute.
subfiles.summary: Randolph recounts Tokugawa’s friendly remarks on U.S. relations, dismissal of war fears involving Russia, defense of Japanese trade, and argument for a stronger defensive fleet. He expects Japan to seek new naval ratios and suggests national pride contributes to its dissatisfaction. He encloses a newspaper account of the speech.

subfiles.title: Japan’s envoy asserts need for defensive navy
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokugawa’s Quebec speech on Japanese naval needs.
subfiles.summary: Reports his call for more destroyers and submarines and disarmament by larger naval powers.

subfiles.summary: Thanks the Ambassador for his Article 10(b) notification.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on delayed Japanese vessel reports

subfiles.about: Compares recent Japanese treaty reports with vessels still unreported.
subfiles.summary: Notes apparent delays in Japanese reporting of several destroyers and submarines.

subfiles.title: Confidential note on Japanese naval reporting
subfiles.about: Discusses the reporting procedure and estimated dates for Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Says the naval attaché received Japanese Navy information and lists approximate construction dates.

subfiles.title: Keel laying of aircraft carrier Soryu

subfiles.summary: States the aircraft carrier is new construction, not a replacement.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Soryu notice

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Soryu’s particulars.

subfiles.title: File note on Texada Island magnetite
subfiles.about: Points to negotiations over Texada Island iron ore exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references despatch 253 in file 842.6351/12.

subfiles.title: Reported Japanese negotiations for British Columbia magnetite
subfiles.from: John K. Davis, American Consul General, Vancouver
subfiles.about: Reports alleged Japanese interest in working and importing Texada Island magnetite.
subfiles.summary: Davis describes the ore deposits and earlier unsuccessful development efforts. He does not know how far the new negotiations have progressed.

subfiles.title: Navy approval of reduction gear quotation
subfiles.about: Allows Westinghouse to quote reduction gears to Japan under specified limits.
subfiles.summary: Permits a bid using commercial or Japanese specifications, excluding U.S. Navy specifications.

subfiles.title: Westinghouse request to quote reduction gears
subfiles.about: Requests permission to quote 25,000 horsepower reduction gears to the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.summary: Promises to withhold U.S. Navy equipment information and supervise Japanese inspectors’ plant visits.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on reduction gear quotation
subfiles.from: Pierrepont Moffat, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Conveys Navy approval of the proposed reduction gear quotation.
subfiles.summary: Approval depends on excluding U.S. Navy specifications. Moffat says no other treaty or statute bars the export.

subfiles.title: Notice to Navy Secretary on Westinghouse reply
subfiles.about: Sends a copy of the State Department’s reply to Westinghouse.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Navy’s February 8 letter on the reduction gear bid.

subfiles.title: Notice to War Secretary on Westinghouse reply
subfiles.about: Sends the War Department the State Department’s reply to Westinghouse.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the letter concerning reduction gears for Japan.

subfiles.title: File note on Japan’s ability to build a large navy
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on an article about Japanese naval finances.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a memorandum discussing Y. K. Karakami’s article.

subfiles.title: Keel laying of destroyer Harusame

subfiles.summary: Lists displacement, dimensions, and gun calibre.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Harusame notice

subfiles.title: Navy acknowledgment of Westinghouse correspondence

subfiles.summary: Confirms receipt of the February 15 correspondence.

subfiles.title: File note on German armaments and Japanese diplomacy
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on German armaments and a conversation with Japan’s Ambassador.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references telegram 64 in file 862.20/766.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese naval press comment
subfiles.about: Points to Japanese press coverage of naval construction, maneuvers, Siam, and espionage.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a report in file 811.21/63.

subfiles.title: Navy approval of cruiser propulsion equipment
subfiles.from: W. H. Standley, Acting Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Approves proposed Westinghouse cruiser propulsion equipment for export to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Approval requires withholding information about equipment supplied to the U.S. Navy.

subfiles.title: Westinghouse request for cruiser propulsion negotiations
subfiles.about: Seeks permission to negotiate a complete cruiser propulsion set for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Proposes adding turbines, condensers, and pumps to previously approved gears.

subfiles.title: State approval of cruiser propulsion equipment
subfiles.from: James Clement Dunn, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Conveys Navy approval of the proposed cruiser propulsion export.
subfiles.summary: The approval bars disclosure of U.S. Navy equipment information. Dunn states that no other treaty or statute restricts the sale.

subfiles.title: Notice to Navy Secretary on cruiser equipment reply
subfiles.about: Sends a copy of State’s reply to Westinghouse.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Standley’s July 22 approval letter.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal of Navy approval for cruiser machinery
subfiles.from: W. H. Standley, Acting Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Withdraws approval of Westinghouse’s proposed cruiser machinery sale pending investigation.
subfiles.summary: The Navy needs to examine design details of the main propulsion machinery.

subfiles.title: State notice of withdrawn approval
subfiles.from: James Clement Dunn, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Informs Westinghouse that Navy approval of the cruiser equipment sale has been withdrawn.
subfiles.summary: The withdrawal lasts pending investigation of machinery design details.

subfiles.title: Notice to Navy Secretary of withdrawn approval reply
subfiles.from: William Phillips, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Sends a copy of State’s withdrawal notice to Westinghouse.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Standley’s August 2 letter.

subfiles.title: Keel laying of destroyer Yamakaze
subfiles.from: A. Uchizawa, for the Japanese Ambassador
subfiles.about: Reports Yamakaze’s May 25 keel laying and specifications.
subfiles.summary: Lists displacement, dimensions, and gun calibre.

subfiles.title: Keel laying of destroyers Kawakaze and Umikaze
subfiles.from: A. Hahie, for the Japanese Ambassador
subfiles.about: Reports the keel laying and common specifications of Kawakaze and Umikaze.
subfiles.summary: Their keels were laid April 25 and May 4, 1935.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of three destroyer notices
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese notices on Yamakaze, Kawakaze, and Umikaze.
subfiles.summary: Thanks the Embassy for Article 10 keel laying particulars.
